subtopics.title: International Affairs and Places
subtopics.summary: This group covers a three-nation defence pact in West Asia, the NATO Ankara Summit 2026, the India-Bangladesh Ganga water sharing treaty and Nauru's new indigenous name. The pact and the summit both concern collective defence, while the treaty and the renaming concern shared resources and national identity.
facts: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement.
Türkiye described the pact as a defence-oriented partnership, not an alliance aimed at a particular country.
An armed attack on one member is to be treated as an attack on all three.
The pact is meant to complement existing regional and international security mechanisms rather than replace them.
The 2025 Pakistan-Saudi Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement was expanded into a trilateral framework.
NATO Ankara Summit 2026 followed the 2025 Hague Summit.
NATO members endorsed the Hague Defence Commitment to spend 5% of GDP on defence by 2035.
The 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty is scheduled to expire in December 2026.
The Farakka Barrage is on the Ganga river at Murshidabad, West Bengal.
Nauru adopted the indigenous name Republic of Naoero to strengthen cultural identity and sovereignty.

subtopics.title: Governance, Welfare and Digital Safety
subtopics.summary: The Indian Statistical Institute Bill 2026 would change ISI's legal status and governance, with the President of India as Visitor. The NCDC (Amendment) Bill 2026 widens direct financing for cooperatives, and PM-VBRY supports first-time employment. Meta's new teen safety rules follow a settlement with 52 State Attorneys General.
facts: The Indian Statistical Institute Bill 2026 was introduced in Lok Sabha and seeks to repeal the ISI Act, 1959.
Under the Bill, the President of India would become the Visitor of the Indian Statistical Institute.
The Visitor can review functioning, order inquiries and issue binding directions.
The existing 33-member Council would be replaced by an 11-member Board of Governors.
The Director would be appointed by the Board with the Visitor's prior approval and would act as chief executive officer.
Under the Bill, central approval would be required only for the first set of regulations.
Parliament passed the National Cooperative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
NCDC can now lend or grant funds directly to any cooperative society, subject to prescribed conditions.
PM-VBRY completed one year, and its implementation period runs from 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2027.
Meta plans default safety limits for teens, including a 2-hour cumulative daily limit across Instagram and Facebook.

subtopics.title: Environment, Energy and Wildlife
subtopics.summary: This group covers elephant and lion conservation, India's low rank in the Environmental Performance Index 2026, and two clean-energy schemes. The wildlife items show conservation efforts, while the index and the energy schemes show how environmental goals are being pursued.
facts: India observed World Elephant Day on 12 August 2026 with the theme 'Bringing the World together to help Elephants'.
A Rs 2,500 crore regional action plan covers Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
Phase II of the Human-Elephant Conflict study covers Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and West Bengal.
India has 33 Elephant Reserves and 150 identified elephant corridors.
The synchronous estimation for 2021-25 put India's wild elephant population at 22,446.
Project Lion was launched on 15 August 2020.
The Asiatic lion population rose from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025.
India ranked 176th of 177 countries in the Environmental Performance Index 2026, and Estonia topped the index.
The Omkareshwar Floating Solar Park is on the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh.
GOBARdhan converts animal waste, crop residue and kitchen waste into compressed biogas and bio-slurry.

subtopics.title: History, Symbols and Personalities
subtopics.summary: This group covers P.C. Mahalanobis and National Statistics Day, the national flag and the role of Pingali Venkayya, and the 1946 Royal Indian Navy Mutiny. The items link science, national symbols and anti-colonial protest. Venkayya's 150th birth anniversary was marked in 2026.
facts: P.C. Mahalanobis is regarded as the Father of Indian Statistics.
He founded Sankhya, India's first statistical journal, in 1933.
He drafted India's 2nd Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), based on his four-sector model.
India designated 29 June as National Statistics Day in 2007.
The 2026 theme of National Statistics Day is 'Unlocking Potential of Administrative Data'.
Pingali Venkayya was born on 2 August 1876 in Krishna, Andhra Pradesh.
In 1921, Venkayya presented a khadi flag design to Mahatma Gandhi at the Congress session in Vijayawada.
The white band on the flag represents peace and truth, and the Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes.
The Royal Indian Navy Mutiny began at HMIS Talwar in Bombay on 18 February 1946.
Rebels in the mutiny organised under a Naval Strike Committee.

subtopics.title: Awards, Science and Agriculture
subtopics.summary: This group covers the Fields Medal 2026, the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal 2026 and India's new popcorn maize hybrid. The award items explain eligibility, frequency and awarding bodies, while the maize item places the crop among India's major food crops.
facts: The Fields Medal 2026 was awarded to Yu Deng, John Pardon, Jacob Tsimerman and Hong Wang.
Hong Wang became the third woman to win the Fields Medal.
The Fields Medal was established in 1936 through the efforts of John Charles Fields.
Fields Medal recipients must be below 40 years of age at the time of the award.
Two to four mathematicians may be honoured in each cycle, and the medal is awarded once every four years.
The Fields Medal is awarded by the International Mathematical Union.
Annapurni Subramaniam, Director of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, Bengaluru, received the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal 2026.
The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal was established in 1990 and is awarded biennially.
The medal was conferred at the 46th Scientific Assembly in Florence, Italy.
India's indigenous, non-GMO popcorn maize hybrid seed was launched at Musunuru, Eluru, Andhra Pradesh.

quizzes.passage: Several developments in international affairs drew attention recently. Three countries in West Asia signed a defence arrangement that aims to strengthen military cooperation among them and to contribute to peace and stability in the region. The arrangement provides a framework for enhanced defence coordination, security cooperation and military interaction. The arrangement reflects a move toward regional ownership of security, in which West Asian nations take primary responsibility for their own defence. A summit of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, held in Türkiye, reviewed defence spending and support for Ukraine. Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to collective defence and to the Washington Treaty. Members also committed to expanding Europe's defence industrial capacity through research centres and skilled workforce development. A river-sharing treaty between India and Bangladesh governs how Ganga waters are shared during the dry season. The treaty is a long-standing arrangement that establishes a formula for distributing water in the lean season. The treaty sets out a mechanism for cooperation between two neighbouring countries over a shared river system. In the Pacific, a small island nation chose to adopt a new formal name to strengthen its cultural identity and national sovereignty. Another item concerns the Ganga treaty's dry-season coverage, which runs from January to 31 May.

questions.q: The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement treats an armed attack against one member as what?
options: A matter for bilateral talks only
A concern limited to the attacked member
An attack on all three members
A matter for the United Nations Security Council

questions.q: The 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty is scheduled to expire in which month and year?
Which body classified the indigenous Naoero language as severely endangered?

Reason (R): The agreement is intended to complement existing regional and international security mechanisms rather than replace them.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

quizzes.passage: Recent international news covered a security pact among three nations and a summit of a large military alliance. The pact brings together its members for enhanced defence coordination, security cooperation and military interaction. The three governments aim to strengthen their ability to deter external aggression. The pact is a framework rather than a replacement for existing structures. Among other items, the summit reviewed defence spending and the defence industrial base in Europe. NATO reaffirmed sustained military, financial and strategic assistance to Ukraine. The alliance's members endorsed a commitment to work toward higher defence spending. NATO was created in 1949 by twelve countries from Europe and North America. A river treaty between India and Bangladesh governs how the Ganga water is shared in the dry season. The treaty's dry season coverage runs from January to 31 May, which is when the sharing arrangement applies. The treaty does not provide a guaranteed minimum flow. A feeder canal diverts part of the Ganga's water into the Hooghly River before it enters Bangladesh. Its institutional mechanism supports cooperation over shared river systems and water resources. In the Pacific, a small island country has changed its formal name to reflect its language and heritage, and it lies near the equator. The name change is meant to preserve its language, which UNESCO has classified as severely endangered.

quizzes.passage: Several governance and welfare measures were in the news this month. A Bill introduced in the Lok Sabha seeks to reform the Indian Statistical Institute, which was founded in 1931 and has its headquarters in Kolkata. The Bill would convert the institute into a statutory body corporate and replace its existing council with a smaller board. Parliament also passed an amendment that widens the financing role of a national body that supports cooperative societies. The body was established in 1963 and its core mandate is to promote and finance cooperative development. The cooperative sector is also addressed by the Constitution, which directs the state to promote voluntary formation of cooperatives. A central employment scheme completed its first year, and it is designed to promote first-time jobs and to support social security coverage. Meanwhile, a social media company announced new default protections for teenage users after a settlement with many state attorneys general in the United States. The protections cover daily use, engagement metrics and the way content is ranked for teen accounts. The founder, Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis, is regarded as the father of Indian statistics. National Statistics Day, observed on 29 June, honours his contributions to the field. The Bill's changes to governance affect how the institute is run and who oversees its functioning.

questions.q: Under the Indian Statistical Institute Bill 2026, who would become the Visitor of the Institute?
options: The Chairperson of the Board of Governors

questions.q: Under the Bill, who appoints the Director of the Indian Statistical Institute?
options: The Board, with the Visitor's prior approval

questions.q: Under the Meta teen safety measures, what is the cumulative daily limit across Instagram and Facebook?

Reason (R): Under the Bill, central approval would be required only for the first set of regulations.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

quizzes.passage: Governance reform and welfare schemes featured in the news recently. A bill in the Lok Sabha would replace the Indian Statistical Institute's governing structure, which is currently a council with 33 members. The institute was founded in 1931 by Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis and began as a statistical laboratory in Kolkata. Parliament also passed an amendment to the law governing a national corporation that promotes cooperative development in agriculture, processing and storage. The Constitution directs the state to promote the voluntary formation and democratic control of cooperatives. A national employment scheme completed one year of operation, offering first-time jobs and incentives to employers. Separately, a social media company announced new default protections for teenage users of its platforms, following a settlement with many state attorneys general in the United States. The company plans to limit daily use, hide engagement counts and restrict late-night access to some features. The bill would also create a formal academic council and a finance committee for the institute. The institute's Director would act as the chief executive officer under the bill. The incentive for employers covers each eligible additional employee for two years, with extended support in manufacturing. Under the same scheme, a one-time incentive is available to employees earning up to a monthly wage limit.

quizzes.passage: Awards and scientific recognition have featured in recent news. A major prize in mathematics was given to a group of mathematicians for exceptional contributions to research, and one of the recipients is a woman. The prize recognises existing achievement in the field as well as the promise of future contributions. The Fields Medal was financed by a trust established at a university in Canada. Earlier winners included mathematicians of Indian origin. Separately, an Indian astrophysics director received a medal from a body that promotes international cooperation in space research. The medal is named after a founder of India's space programme. The Indian Institute of Astrophysics is based in Bengaluru. The COSPAR body was established in 1958 and is affiliated with the International Science Council. The COSPAR award is a medal conferred at an international assembly of scientists. In agriculture, a new seed product was launched in a southern Indian state. The seed was launched at a processing facility run by a popcorn business. The seed is indigenous, and it does not involve genetically modified material. Maize is a major crop in India, and production was reported in millions of tonnes for 2025-26. Each of these items relates to a different field, from mathematics to space research to agriculture.

quizzes.passage: Awards and science news featured among recent developments. A prestigious prize in mathematics was given to four mathematicians this year for exceptional research. The prize honours existing achievement and the promise of future work, and recipients must be younger than forty at the time of the award. Another award went to a senior astrophysics figure from India, who received a medal recognising research by scientists from developing countries. The medal is awarded every two years by a body linked to space science, and it was presented at a major international scientific assembly. The medal's name honours a founder of India's space programme. In farming news, a new popcorn maize hybrid was launched in a southern Indian state. The seed is indigenous, is not genetically modified, and was developed through a partnership between a national research institute and a company. India's maize production was reported at millions of tonnes for the 2025-26 season, and the crop is grown across several states. The prize's recipients also include mathematicians of Indian origin, honoured in earlier years. The medal was conferred on a woman scientist. Earlier recipients of the award from India were honoured in several different years, with the most recent in 2024. The COSPAR medal honours contributions to space research.
